title: Harden TP collectives: async error propagation + timeouts to prevent silent stalls
creator: Noah Patel
project: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes (Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Background / Problem
- We have multi-GPU tensor-parallel (TP) hangs under sustained load where a TP worker group enters a stuck state without surfacing a clear error.
- A common failure mode is NCCL/collective async errors (or transport issues) that do not immediately propagate to the runtime scheduler; collectives appear to “wait forever” and we keep assigning work to a group that will never make forward progress.

Goal
- Ensure collective-layer failures are detected and surfaced quickly enough to:
  1) stop scheduling new work onto a doomed TP group,
  2) quarantine/reset the TP group (handled in ENG-2407/ENG-2402), and
  3) return deterministic errors upstream (rather than silent stalls / long tail timeouts).

In scope
- Add periodic async error checks for collective operations (NCCL async error state), and treat detected errors as terminal for the in-flight request and TP group.
- Add explicit timeouts for collectives / rendezvous points where we otherwise wait indefinitely.
- Define abort policy (what do we abort, when, and how) compatible with correctness:
  - When to abort the TP group vs abort a single request.
  - How to ensure we don’t keep a partially-failed communicator alive.
- Ensure the scheduler sees a single “collective failure” signal quickly, with enough context for logs/metrics.

Out of scope
- Switching comm backend or major refactor of TP architecture.
- Customer networking/driver remediation.

Proposed behavior (high level)
- Runtime has a per-TP-group collective “health” channel that receives errors from the collective path.
- During collective waits, we periodically poll for async error state and/or completion (without blocking indefinitely).
- If async error is detected OR timeout threshold is exceeded:
  - Fail current request with a typed error (CollectiveTimeout / CollectiveAsyncError).
  - Mark TP group as unhealthy (handoff to scheduler state machine in ENG-2402).
  - Trigger quarantine path (ENG-2407) and prevent new work from landing.

Abort policy (initial)
- Default: abort at TP-group scope (failure domain = TP group) once we see a collective async error or timeout on any rank.
  - Rationale: once a communicator is poisoned, continuing can wedge subsequent requests and cause prolonged stalls.
- Request-only abort is allowed ONLY for explicit request cancellation before the collective begins (handled in ENG-2403). Once a collective is entered, failures are treated as TP-group failures.
- For Hosted (large pools): aggressive quarantine to limit blast radius.
- For Dedicated: configurable thresholds with conservative defaults; allow opt-in more aggressive behavior after canary results.

Tuning knobs / flags (expected)
- collective_async_error_poll_interval_ms (default: 50ms)
- collective_hard_timeout_ms (default: 15000ms for Hosted; 30000ms for Dedicated; Private TBD)
- collective_soft_timeout_ms (optional; if exceeded, emit warning log + metric but don’t abort yet)
- collective_abort_policy (group|host) (initially group only; host restart handled separately by watchdog/quarantine work)

Metrics / observability (minimal requirements for this ticket)
- runtime.tp.collective.async_error_detected_total{op,model,gpu_type}
- runtime.tp.collective.timeout_total{op,model,gpu_type,threshold=soft|hard}
- runtime.tp.collective.wait_ms_histogram{op,model}
- runtime.tp.group.abort_reason_total{reason=collective_async_error|collective_timeout}
- Structured log on abort with:
  - tp_group_id, rank, op, elapsed_ms, request_id (if available), model_id, nccl_error_code (if available)

Acceptance criteria
- In repro suite (ENG-2405) scenarios that previously hung indefinitely:
  - runtime detects condition and aborts within hard_timeout_ms + 2*poll_interval.
  - scheduler receives the failure and stops dispatching new work to that TP group (validated via existing state metrics / logs; enforcement may land in ENG-2402).
- No increase in false positive aborts above agreed threshold in canary (tracked in watchdog experiments doc; initial target <0.1% of TP groups/day in Hosted canary).
- Perf impact:
  - <1% throughput regression on standard TP benchmark suite; polling must not introduce global synchronization.

Implementation notes / constraints
- Avoid calling blocking NCCL APIs on critical CUDA stream; ensure polling does not stall kernel execution.
- Ensure error checks are rank-consistent enough to avoid half the ranks proceeding (use a shared abort signal / check before launching next collective).
- Be careful with request cancellation: if a request is canceled mid-collective, treat as collective failure only if it causes collective mismatch; otherwise cancellation should not poison communicator.

Rollout
- Land behind feature flag default-off in runtime-1.19 pre-release builds.
- Enable in Hosted canary pools first with conservative hard_timeout.
- Expand to 10% Hosted, then 50%, then default-on.
- Dedicated: opt-in per cluster with documented defaults; support can advise customers experiencing hangs.

Testing
- Unit test: simulated collective wait path triggers timeout and emits expected error type + metrics.
- Integration test: fault injection from repro harness (rank delay / forced NCCL error) leads to abort + quarantine signal.

Owner notes
- Grace Kim driving implementation with review from Hiro Tanaka (collectives) and Rafael Mendes (SRE guardrails).
comments: 2025-02-17 (Noah Patel): Creating this as P0 out of Sev1 learnings. We need to stop the ‘silent stall’ mode; even a controlled abort is better than indefinite hangs. Please align abort policy with ADR-0147 so SRE can build clean alerting + runbooks.

2025-02-18 (Hiro Tanaka): Agree on TP-group failure domain for async errors. We’ve seen poisoned communicators where the *next* request wedges, so request-scoped retries are risky. Let’s keep it simple: once any rank reports an async error / hard timeout, flip group health -> unhealthy and let scheduler quarantine. Also: polling interval should be small but not per-kernel; we can do it in the collective wait loop only.

2025-02-20 (Grace Kim): Drafted implementation approach: (1) wrap collective launch + wait in a small state object that tracks start_ts + op name; (2) every poll_interval: check completion + call ncclCommGetAsyncError (or equivalent wrapper); (3) if error, return Status::CollectiveAsyncError; (4) if elapsed > hard timeout, return Status::CollectiveTimeout. Will wire to scheduler via existing ‘tp_group_fault’ channel (new enum value).

2025-02-21 (Rafael Mendes): SRE ask: ensure we emit a single, rate-limited ERROR log per TP group transition to unhealthy. During incidents, log volume killed us. Also please include tp_group_id and rank in log fields (structured) for correlation. For canary gating: we’ll watch tp_group_resets + 5xx + timeout rate.

2025-02-24 (Grace Kim): Opened PR-18455 with polling + timeout. Added new metrics counters + histogram; defaults set to 15s hard timeout for Hosted. Need to confirm Dedicated default (30s?) with Sofia/Lena because long sequences can legitimately take longer.

2025-02-25 (Sofia Ivanova): Scheduler side: we can consume the ‘tp_group_fault’ signal and mark group unhealthy; hard enforcement (no new work to quarantined groups) is in ENG-2402 PR-18432. For this ticket, just make sure the fault signal is synchronous and not dropped on cancellation path.

2025-02-27 (Isabella Rossi): Perf sanity: polling adds a branch in the wait path; microbench on A100 shows no measurable regression (<0.2%). Please avoid additional device sync; keep everything on host-side check loop.

2025-03-01 (Hiro Tanaka): Code review on PR-18455: please ensure we map NCCL error codes into a stable error class for dashboards (don’t log raw strings only). Also: soft timeout should warn once per request, not on every poll tick.

2025-03-03 (Grace Kim): Addressed feedback: added stable error_code field, rate-limited logs, and soft-timeout single warning. PR updated; pending final approval + merge window for runtime-1.19 hotfix branch.

2025-03-04 (Connor O'Brien): Release note dependency: once merged, please update runtime-1.19 TP stability fixes note with new flags and defaults (poll interval + hard timeout). We need a clear statement on behavior change: ‘hangs become fast-fail + auto quarantine’.
